Re: The Flood On The Holm

The Scott Skinner tunes are ‘The Auld Wheel’, as iris eve identifies above, ‘The Spinning Wheel’ and ‘The Bride’s Reel. Not all of them, as that would give 6 parts instead of 5, and not any of them exactly the same, of course. I think it;’s probably fair to say that John Doherty created something of his own out of them. That’s the “folk process” at work, I guess…
‘The Spinnin’ Wheel’: first and second parts
First part of ‘The Auld Wheel’: third part
Second part of ‘The Bride’s Reel’: fourth part
First part of ‘The Bride’s Reel’ (sort of..): fifty part..
Interestingly ‘The Bride’s Reel’ and ‘The Auld Wheel’ appear next to one another at the bottom of page 7 of ‘The Scottish Violinist’, though ‘The Spinning’ Wheel‘ is back on the bottom of page 3. But did John Doherty read music? I expect that someone must know. It doesn’t say in Caoimhin MacAoidh’s book ’Between The Jigs and the Reels’; but it does say that he was exposed to commercial recordings by James Scott Skinner, and that these made the greatest impression on him.

The Flood On The Holm, X:4

This is a version I transcribed from a local Nashville piper, who adapted it from a very old Robbie Hannan recording. According to this piper, Robbie recorded the tune a few different ways, and he always preferred his earliest recording. I’ve included some of the variations from our piper’s playing, which I think sound very nice in this somewhat “open” tune!

↳ Posted by Kocopelly on March 13th, 2026.
